The source feedback indicated that these findings, along with compensatory hyperaeration of the remaining right lung lobes, supported the diagnosis. The source feedback indicated that while automated tools reported non-specific findings like mild cardiomegaly or lung opacity, the definitive radiographic evidence supporting the answer was a subtle Westermark sign in the right hemithorax, suggestive of chronic vascular obstruction rather than acute embolism or parenchymal disease. This highlights that in Takayasu arteritis, chest X-ray findings may be subtle signs of chronic vascular compromise (such as oligemia or compensatory changes) rather than overt acute pathology, requiring careful interpretation beyond standard automated reports which may miss specific vascular signs."]
